title: Freedom is all you need
comment: 26 pages. This manuscript was developed, produced, and edited entirely by humans
summary: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

title: Invariant rings of Frobenius polarization operators and normal cores of subgroups
summary: For a proper subgroup $H$ of a finite group $G$, we determine the common kernel, or invariant ring, of the Frobenius polarization operators corresponding to the elements of $G\setminus H$. We show that the invariant rings defined by the left and right polarization operators coincide and depend only on the normal core $N=\operatorname{Core}_G(H)$. We construct polynomials $P_Ω$ indexed by the orbits of the conjugation action of $G$ on $\widehat N$ and prove that they form an algebraically independent generating set for the invariant ring. We also show that inclusion of these invariant rings as subrings of $\mathbb C[\mathbf{x}]$ is equivalent to inclusion of the corresponding normal cores. For an arbitrary subgroup $H$, we give a factorization of the group determinant in terms of these polynomials. This factorization generalizes Frobenius' group determinant theorem and reduces to its factorization when $H=G$. When $G$ is abelian, each $P_Ω$ is a specialization of the group determinant of the quotient group $G/H$. Finally, we establish a Capelli identity for each $P_Ω$ and compute the coefficient polynomial obtained by applying a constant-coefficient differential operator to its powers.

title: Linear support bounds for supercuspidal matrix coefficients of p-adic groups
summary: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. For any standard congruence tower $K_{\bullet}=(K_n)$ in $\mathbf{G}(F)$, supercuspidal matrix coefficients between $K_n$-fixed vectors are supported in an adjoint ball of radius $an+b_{K_{\bullet}}$, compact modulo the center, with $a$ depending only on $F$ and $\mathbf{G}$. When $\mathbf{G}(F)$ is non-compact modulo its center, the linear dependence on $n$ is optimal. In algebraic families we obtain a uniform radius $An+Bk+C+\operatorname{val}_{F}(N)$, where $k$ bounds the logarithmic height of the parameter. We deduce a sharp linear bound for the exponent in Bernstein's stabilization theorem. For quasi-split classical groups, we also remove the dyadic level restriction in the limit multiplicity theorem.

title: The non symmetric Hikita conjecture
summary:
We construct local and global comparison maps for the Hikita conjecture in quiver gauge theories and study their analogues for finite non symmetric Cartan pairs. The construction uses quiver Hecke description of Coulomb branch and microlocal geometry. It yields comparison maps from B-algebras to the cohomology of some Lagrangians of quiver varieties.
  For arbitrary symmetric types, the local and global comparison maps are surjective and are isomorphisms under a B-algebra dimension bound. In finite non symmetric types, the local image is the image of the Kirwan map, i.e., the tautological subalgebra. It can be proper. Under some assumptions we also construct a non symmetric global comparison map.
  Crystal theoretic methods identify the set of nonempty Lagrangians with the set of isomorphism classes of simple modules of the category $\mathscr O$ of the Coulomb branch, and proves that the Lagrangians are nonempty for $\ell$-dominant $\ell$-highest weights.
  The proof uses microlocal modules of Coulomb branches that we define. We prove they form integral bases of the Grothendieck group of the category $\mathscr O$, with Jordan-Hölder multiplicities given by characteristic cycles.
  In symmetric type we prove an isomorphism between based quasimap modules at homogeneous polarized points of quiver varieties and co-specialized microlocal modules. The proof uses hyperbolic restriction and Braden's theorem. We conjecture an extension to all homogeneous points and a relative version.

title: Equivariant extension of $I_N$-finite tempered distributions on real flag varieties
summary: Let $G$ be a real linear reductive group and let $P=L_PU_P$ and $Q=LN$ be parabolic subgroups. For a Casselman--Wallach representation $F$ of $L_P$, let $\mathcal{E}_F$ be the unnormalized homogeneous tempered bundle on $G/P$ induced from $F$. We prove that every $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on a $Q$-stable Nash open subset of $G/P$ extends to an $I_N$-finite tempered distribution on $G/P$.

title: Nonreduced Finkelberg-Mirković Schubert schemes
summary: We develop an effective numerical criterion ($θ$-minimality) to detect the nonreducedness of Finkelberg-Mirković (FM) Schubert schemes via tangent-space comparisons at arbitrary torus-fixed points. We completely classify the dominant coweights admitting $θ$-minimal pairs. As an application, we obtain nonreduced FM Schubert schemes in every type other than $A_n$ and $C_n$. In particular, every nontrivial FM Schubert scheme of type $E_8$ is nonreduced. In type $D_n$, we show that some nonreduced FM Schubert schemes and their corresponding spherical Schubert varieties have the same tangent space at the base point. Our methods use the Frenkel-Kac construction of basic representations and Segal-Sugawara operators.

title: Recursive Relations for Categorified Young Symmetrizers in Type $\mathbb{B}$
summary: The category of bounded-above chain complexes of Soergel bimodules of any finite type $\mathbb{X}_n$ contains a symmetrizer complex $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{X}_n}$ which kills non-identity Soergel bimodules up to homotopy. It has been shown in previous work that, in type $\mathbb{A}$, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_{n+1}}$ can be obtained as a semi-infinite extension between copies of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{A}_n}$ and its product with a Jucys-Murphy complex. We prove an analogous recursion holds between the symmetrizers for type $\mathbb{B}_n$ and $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$. Following the method of the result in type $\mathbb{A}$, we then use this to prove that the cohomology ring of the endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{P}_{\mathbb{B}_n}$ is a polynomial ring.

title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
summary: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

title: Demazure-Lusztig type operators and correspondences on Kato Catalan varieties
summary: We study the integral equivariant cohomology rings of Kato Catalan varieties $\mathscr{X}_Ψ$ associated with arbitrary root ideals $Ψ$ in type $A$. These varieties are smooth projective compactifications of the vector subbundles $T^*_Ψ\mathcal{B}$ of the cotangent bundle of the complete flag variety $\mathcal{B}$. Let $K$ denote the product of the general linear group (or its maximal torus) with the loop rotation torus $\mathbb{C}^\times$. We give an explicit presentation of $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_Ψ;\mathbb{Z})$ with relations expressed in terms of divided difference and Demazure-Lusztig type operators. Furthermore, for every simple reflection preserving $Ψ\cup(-Ψ)$, we construct a geometric realization of the associated Demazure-Lusztig type operator on $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_Ψ;\mathbb{Z})$ via correspondences. These correspondences yield a faithful graded action of the subalgebra of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra generated by these reflections and the polynomial subalgebra. For the maximal root ideal $Ψ=Δ^+$, our construction recovers the cohomological counterpart of the $K$-theoretic Steinberg correspondences of Cautis and Kamnitzer.

title: Opposite filtrations on the parabolic compactified Jacobian
summary: We show that the Hikita filtration on the cohomology of the parabolic compactified Jacobian of the plane curve singularity $x^m=y^n$, $(m,n)=1$, is opposite to the perverse filtration in a precise sense. This implies the parabolic Hilb-vs-Quot conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19633, and consequently the main conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115 for these singularities. The new ingredient is an analysis of how the Bott-Mitchell filtration on the homology of the affine Grassmannian of $SL_n$ relates to both of the above filtrations.

title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
summary: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $ξ$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

title: Cohomology of twisted tensor products over commutative rings
summary: Over a commutative ground ring, cohomology of a twisted tensor product of two rings mixes their cohomology via the twisting. We focus on bicharacter twistings and give explicit descriptions when the ground ring is itself a module. We state our main results for ground rings that are hereditary and contain roots of unity corresponding to finite grading groups. As a class of examples, we compute cohomology rings of Taft orders over cyclotomic integers.

title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
comment: 17 pages, comments welcome! v2: minor notational update
summary: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\mathscr{C}$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
comment: 13 pages. We have corrected the errors in Theorem 1.2 and Section 1.2
summary: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
comment: 33 pages including 16 pages of a Magma program
summary: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $Λ$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
comment: 11 pages; v2 adds an acknowledgements section; v3 adds a remark on p.8 and a declaration of AI use
summary: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

title: Euler characters for general linear Lie superalgebra
summary: M. Gorelik and Th. Heidersdors in the papers \cite{GH} investigated Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ and $\frak{osp}(m.2n)$. In the present paper we also investigate Euler characters for Lie superalgebra $\frak{gl}(m,n)$ but we use a different approach and our results are formulated in different terms.

title: Lie Algebra Decomposition Classes for Reductive Algebraic Groups in Arbitrary Characteristic
summary: In this paper, we investigate the decomposition classes of the Lie algebras of connected reductive algebraic groups, over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We extend some results proved previously under restrictions on the characteristic, including a formula for the dimension of a decomposition class, and introduce Levi-type decomposition classes to account for some of the difficulties encountered in bad characteristic. We also establish properties of Lusztig--Spaltenstein induction of non-nilpotent orbits, such as parabolic independence, extending the known results for nilpotent orbits. Finally, we determine the covering relation for the closure order on decomposition classes, in the case of good characteristic.

title: Irreducible representations of pointed Hopf algebras of type $A_2$
summary: We classify the irreducible representations of a family of finite-dimensional pointed liftings $H_λ$ of the Nichols algebra associated with the diagram $A_2$ with parameter $q=-1$. We show that these algebras have infinite representation type and construct an indecomposable $H_λ$-module of dimension $n$ for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Finally, we study a semisimple category $\underline{\operatorname{Rep}} H_λ$ arising as a quotient of $\operatorname{Rep} H_λ$.

title: An introduction to the symmetric group algebra
comment: 836 pages. Lots of details (should be undergrad-friendly). Includes a SageMath tutorial (sec. 3.14). Ancillary files are a note on YJM elements, a note on the Peel exact sequence and talk slides on counting tableaux. Updates will appear on https://darijgrinberg.gitlab.io/t/24s/ . v2 corrects errors and adds a few examples and exercises. Comments are welcome!
summary:
This is an introduction to the group algebras of the symmetric groups, written for a quarter-long graduate course. After recalling the definition of group algebras (and monoid algebras) in general, as well as basic properties of permutations, we introduce several families of elements in the symmetric group algebras $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ such as the Young--Jucys--Murphy elements, the (sign-)integrals and the conjugacy class sums. Then comes a chapter on group actions and representations in general, followed by the core of this text: a study of the representations of symmetric groups (i.e., of left $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$-modules), including the classical theory of Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers. We prove in detail the main facts including the characterization of irreducible representations (in characteristic $0$), the Garnir relations, the standard basis theorem, the description of duals of Specht modules, and the hook length formula, as well as a number of less known results. Finally, we describe several bases of $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ that arise from the study of Specht modules, including the Murphy cellular bases.
  The methods used are elementary and computational. We aim to assume as little as possible of the base ring $\mathbf{k}$, and to use as little as possible from representation theory (nothing more advanced than Maschke and Jordan--Hölder).
  Over 100 exercises (without solutions) are scattered through the text.

title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
comment: 53 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Minor changes according to referees' suggestions
summary:
Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types.
  To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.

title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente à la formule des traces en caractéristique p>0
summary: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.

title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
comment: 24 pages, 7 figures. v2: updated abstract and introduction; collected some results in a new Theorem 6.4
summary: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $Δ_ξ$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.
